faq.q: What should the Amazon main image show?
faq.a: The main image is the product on pure white, filling most of the square, with no words, logos, or props. Keep a spec line for a later image, and publish the file in Seller Central after you check it. Make the long side large enough for zoom, then confirm the current rule before you upload.

faq.q: What happens if a photo breaks those rules?
faq.a: A main photo that still shows the room can be held back, and the listing can leave search until you replace that file. A prop can sit on a later image, not on the main one.

faq.q: How do I get a white main image from a normal photo?
faq.a: Upload the photo you already have and put the product on white. The old background comes off, the edges stay with the product, and you download a finished file. A photo is 24 credits, shown before you start.

faq.q: Can I prepare many Amazon photos in one run?
faq.a: Yes. Send the whole line through one batch, lifestyle frames included. Each file spends credits, the cost shows first, and a failed job returns those credits. You can also run that batch through the API.

faq.q: Can my catalog tool prepare the Amazon images?
faq.a: Yes. When a new product is saved, your catalog tool can request the image through the API. You choose when it goes into Seller Central. We never sign in to the seller account.

faq.q: What other images should I add to an Amazon listing?
faq.a: A close-up, a sense of size, and the item in use. The mug can sit in a hand so the shopper sees the scale.

faq.q: Can I put words on the pictures?
faq.a: Add the words yourself after download, and only on images after the main one. The main image stays free of badges and slogans.

faq.q: Can I make a video for the listing?
faq.a: Yes. A video is its own job at 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds, costing 24, 40, 60, or 120 credits.

faq.q: Will you upload the photos into Amazon for me?
faq.a: No. Download the files and add them in Seller Central yourself. We do not connect to your seller login.
